subject: Clarify: per-request granularity & first-month minimum waiver

Subject: Clarify: per-request granularity & first-month minimum waiver

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — the model latency looked great. Before we kick off the pilot I have two quick billing questions that will affect our internal forecasting and procurement:

1) How do you meter long streaming requests? For example, we’ll be sending a 20k-token document to be summarized and then an interactive stream back to the user. Do you bill per-request tokenized length (input + output) and round per-call, or do you aggregate multiple calls for the same session?

2) What are your rounding/minimums for short generation calls? We have many micro-interactions (user clicks that request 8–30 token completions). If you have a minimum per-call or quantum rounding it materially changes our unit economics.

Finally, is Redwood willing to waive any per-call minimums or provide an overage credit for the first month of the pilot while we stabilize traffic? Our procurement team prefers a short-term waiver rather than negotiating a larger committed discount up front.

Could you send a short example invoice or sample calculations for two scenarios: a) monthly steady-state (50k tokens/day, split 80/20 input/output) and b) bursty pilot month with many sub-30-token calls?

Appreciate the help — we want to move quickly once we understand the math.

Best,
Amira Khan
Head of AI, FinEdge

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Amira Khan <amira@finedge.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-request granularity & first-month minimum waiver

Hi Amira — thanks for the clear asks, and great to hear the demo was useful. Short answers up front: we meter at token-level, but there are two different behaviors to be aware of that affect rounding and apparent minimums. Below is a concise explanation plus two simple worked examples — happy to walk through live.

How we meter (high level):
- Base unit: tokens (input + output). Every call is tokenized and charged based on tokens consumed.
- Per-call rounding: for standard non-streamed generation calls we round each call up to the nearest 16-token quantum.
- Streaming behavior: for streaming responses we meter the continuous output stream and accumulate tokens over the stream; we round the streamed total up to the nearest 64-token quantum. This avoids frequent micro-charges for long streaming sessions.
- Session aggregation: when requests use the same session_id within a rolling 5-minute window we collapse those into a session bundle for metering purposes (helps interactive back-and-forths). The bundle is billed as the sum of tokens (rounded as above) rather than charging each micro-call separately.

Minimums and waivers:
- There is no hard per-customer monthly minimum by default. However, per-call quantum rounding can create effective minimums for very short calls (e.g., a 6-token output billed as 16 tokens).
- For pilots we can grant a one-time first-month waiver of per-call rounding for calls under 32 output tokens (we’ll bill actual tokens instead of the 16/64 quantum for those calls). We typically limit waivers to avoid abuse; see below for suggested guardrails.

Worked examples (high level):
A) Steady-state (50k tokens/day, 80/20 in/out):
- Daily tokens: 50k -> monthly ~1.5M tokens.
- Rounding impact negligible at scale (quantum effect <0.5% of total).
- Estimated monthly bill: tokens * unit_price (I’ll include numbers if you share target SKU).

B) Bursty pilot (lots of <30-token calls):
- If no waiver: many micro-calls will be rounded to 16 tokens each -> apparent 3–4x delta on tiny calls.
- With the first-month waiver (calls under 32 tokens billed actual): this gap disappears for the initial pilot period.

Internal note: Ben / Vivek — can you confirm commercial permission to offer the waiver described (first-month suppression of per-call rounding on outputs <32 tokens) and a one-time overage credit threshold? Also confirm whether we want to pair the waiver with a modest prepaid commit (e.g., $5k pilot credit) to protect against overage abuses.

Amira — I’ve CC’d Ben (pricing) and Vivek (product). If you want I can produce the two sample invoices you requested (I’ll need a target unit price per 1k tokens; I can also run the scenarios at our standard pilot rate if that’s easiest).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Folks — quick rec on commercial stance:

1) Approve one-time pilot waiver as Priyom described: waive per-call rounding for outputs <32 tokens for the first 30 days of the pilot. We should require a simple pilot prepay or card on file to cover any extreme usage (recommend $5k nonrefundable credit).
2) Offer a 50% overage credit on anything >150% of the forecasted monthly usage for the first month (this protects FinEdge against runaway bursts we didn’t anticipate).
3) Limit waiver to API keys used for the pilot and disable after 30 days automatically. Add logging to the billing event so CS can audit.

Suggested contract language snippet for SOW / pilot addendum:
"Redwood will temporarily suppress per-call rounding on output tokens less than 32 tokens for the initial 30-day pilot period for the API key(s) identified in Appendix A. If monthly usage exceeds 150% of the forecasted volume during the pilot, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the overage amount, up to a maximum credit of $10,000."

I’ve attached a redline of the SOW with the pilot language and a sample usage CSV that we can use to generate the two invoice examples. If Priyom is happy, we can email Amira the concession and the two sample invoices (standard and bursty).

—Ben

- Bursty pilot (100k micro-calls @ 20 tokens output): without waiver would bill ~100k * 16 = 1.6M tokens (appears expensive). With waiver billed actual ~2M tokens total -> much lower effective cost on micro-calls.
